commits.message:
Disabled text is held under what muted text shows as an export draws dim, never vanishing into the ground (rich-palette-xovz.qg7)

Review (medium): the bound assumed dimmed muted stood at its floor, and the
fallback dimmed the faintest slot to near-invisibility. dimShown in
export-lines is now the one reading of SGR dim's strength; writeText weighs
every slot plain then dimmed against it, and the test measures through it.
HELD_UNDER is built once; floorOn and textOn docs say what indexed depths do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Disabled text goes under what dimmed muted text can show, not its assumed floor, and asIs drops the ordering at every depth (rich-palette-xovz.qg7)

Review (high): where muted was dimmed, disabled was measured under textFloor
alone and could take muted's own slot undimmed (catppuccin-latte at sixteen
colors). The bound is now the lesser of the floor and the slot; with no slot
under it, disabled is the faintest slot dimmed, not muted's color. The over
lookup goes through the writeText memo.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Disabled text is written under the slot muted text takes at every indexed depth (rich-palette-xovz.qg7)

At 256 and sixteen colors, slotted held foreground-muted only to textFloor, so
muted and disabled often shared a slot or inverted (VGA defaults over bundled
palettes x every role ground: 932/3427 missed the 0.25 margin at sixteen, 9 at
256). Disabled text, which has no floor, now takes a slot HELD_PAST_MARGIN under
muted's, or muted's color dimmed where none is; under dimmed muted, its floor
stands in for the contrast. Raising muted instead would lift it to body-text
strength at sixteen colors.

ink() already took the frame's depth (themed-widget.ts), and widget labels at
indexed depths are covered by test/widgets/terminal-contrast.test.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

A filled row places its right-to-left line itself, so no option travels to tell text where it stands (rich-control-codes-xh4n.yws) (#593)

* A right-to-left row says where it stands on the frame, and whoever fills the row places it, so no option travels to tell text (rich-control-codes-xh4n.yws)

Text stamps an unplaced right-to-left row with Style.edge (the row and the
width it was laid out in); Segment.leadingFill is the one reader, and Padding,
Layout, Viewport, scroll, Console.print and paint's frame fit read it.
PASSES_EDGE, passingOptions, fillingOptions, renderFilling and renderPassing
are deleted, so a user's own wrapper hands the row on with nothing to know.
Pretty, JSON, Traceback and the strips set their own lines (Segment.settled).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* A holder that sets its own rows settles them, and one that splices rows fills them first (rich-control-codes-xh4n.yws)

Review of #593: a Tree's root label and a Syntax line moved to the right
edge under a filler; a change between two right-to-left texts and a row
under an open overlay lost their place mid-transition; the caret was found
before the leading fill. Tree and Syntax settle their rows, ChangeFrame and
WidgetApp fill before splicing, paint finds the caret on the placed row,
and leadingFill walks a row once without allocating.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* A change's spliced row carries the new row's stamp, so whoever holds the change places it (rich-control-codes-xh4n.yws)

Review of #593 (medium): filling both sides inside ChangeFrame made a
change act as a filler, so a crossfade label in a Tree moved to the right
edge. The spliced row now stands as the new row does, its old side filled
to the new row's width, and Segment.rowEdge is the one reader of the stamp.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* A row's stamp records the cells its text drew, so a window or crop cut from it is never moved (rich-control-codes-xh4n.yws)

Review of #593 (high, second pass): a scroll window cut from a
right-to-left row kept the row's stamp and was pushed toward its
holder's right edge; a change from right-to-left to left-to-right text
kept the old cells' stamp mid-change. RowEdge carries the row's drawn
length in place of an identity field nobody read, rowEdge refuses a row
that no longer has it, Segment.stamped clears when the new row names no
edge, and text stamps through it. Stale comment and blank lines left by
the PASSES_EDGE removal go.
